newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-WILSON NAMED AS WALLABY CAPTAIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WILSON NAMED AS WALLABY CAPTAIN.

text.p: Flanker David Wilson will captain Australia in a test for the first time in Saturday's Tri-Nations match with New Zealand after the Wallabies' double injury setback on Tuesday.
Regular skipper John Eales and flanker Matt Cockbain were ruled out of the Dunedin clash after sustaining injuries in training.
"This has probably been the worst week I have ever experienced in my career as a coach," Wallaby trainer Greg Smith told reporters.
Australia must beat New Zealand and then defeat South Africa in Pretoria on August 23 to prevent the All Blacks from retaining the Tri-Nations title.
The Wallabies have never won a test match in Dunedin and have lost their last six encounters against the All Blacks.

The loss of Eales and Cockbain added to Smith's problems in the forwards after number eight Daniel Manu withdrew last weekend because of a shoulder injury suffered during the 32-20 win over South Africa in Brisbane 10 days ago.
Veteran Troy Coker will come into the side at the back of the scrum, while lock John Langford will make his test debut as Eales's replacement.
Flanker Fili Finau was promoted from the reserves bench to fill the gap left by Cockbain, who sustained mild concussion in a training mishap on Tuesday.
Wilson, a former Queensland captain, led Australia in one mid-week match on their European tour late last year in his only previous experience in the job.
His main rivals for the role -- fly-half Tim Horan and full-back Matt Burke -- are both unavailable because of long-term injuries, adding further to Australia's woes.
Eales, the only forward to play in all of Australia's six tests this season, damaged knee ligaments in training on Monday and a fitness test 24 hours later confirmed his worst fears.
"It (the knee) would definitely not be right to play this weekend," said Eales, whose presence will be sorely missed, particularly in the line-out.
Langford, a surprise choice ahead of the more experienced Garrick Morgan, will join ACT Brumbies team-mate Owen Finegan in the second row.
Smith delayed a decision on whether Andrew Blades would replace Andrew Heath at tighthead prop.

Australia: 15-Stephen Larkham; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan; 8-Troy Coker, 7-David Wilson (captain), 6-Fili Finau, 5-John Langford, 4-Owen Finegan, 3-Andrew Blades or Andrew Heath, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.
